summary: Configured a persistent, legacy-compatible SSH tunnel from node2 loopback port 9082 to node1 loopback port 9081. The tunnel self-recovers, remains inaccessible through cluster IPs, preserves the supplied files, and survived sequential restarts of both nodes.
actions_performed: Added SysV startup for node1’s loopback-only inventory service.
Generated a dedicated RSA tunnel credential and restricted it to forwarding only to 127.0.0.1:9081.
Added a SysV-managed SSH supervisor on node2 with keepalives and automatic reconnection.
Verified recovery after terminating the active SSH connection.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.
Confirmed Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic remain installed.

evidence.requirement: Node1 endpoint remains loopback-only on TCP 9081 and supplied files are preserved
evidence.summary: The original file hashes remain unchanged; node1 listens only on 127.0.0.1:9081 and returns the supplied status document.

evidence.requirement: Persistent SSH tunnel exposes the endpoint on node2 loopback port 9082
evidence.summary: The SysV-managed SSH tunnel listens only on 127.0.0.1:9082 and returns the inventory status document.

evidence.requirement: Other cluster hosts cannot directly access either application listener
evidence.summary: Connections to node1:9081 and node2:9082 through their cluster addresses failed, including after both restarts.

evidence.requirement: Tunnel recovers after a brief SSH connection interruption
evidence.summary: After terminating SSH PID 4266, the unchanged supervisor created PID 4320 and restored the loopback endpoint without manual recreation.

evidence.requirement: Installed operating-system release and kernel are retained
evidence.summary: Both nodes remain on Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic.
Healthy baseline boot ID 44da914f-ec19-451f-aae9-7bd4797978bf was captured, reboot acknowledged, boot ID changed to 61d2be4e-b3ef-488b-9887-b42efc259526, and the application plus tunnel recovered.

Healthy baseline boot ID 1bf5fc7a-964f-4328-995d-9b4284e48feb was captured, reboot acknowledged, boot ID changed to 153bfca9-37b2-4fa3-888d-124dabe7ca96, and the supervised tunnel recovered automatically.
